title: Mid-Pliocene Warm Period
summary: From about 3.3 to 3.0 million years ago Earth had atmospheric carbon dioxide similar to today's, 360 to 420 parts per million by NOAA's account, and a global mean temperature 2.5 to 4.0 degrees C above the late 19th century. Sea level stood roughly 5 to 25 metres higher, and the northern treeline sat 4 to 10 degrees of latitude farther poleward.

uncertainty.note: Both sources give 3.3 to 3.0 million years ago. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

paleo.not_applicable: Global climate interval; no type site is cited.

importance.justification: The most recent interval with CO2 near present levels, widely used to study a warmer climate.
